regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.claim: Presentations of the indications omit specific patient populations and administration in combination with other chemotherapies; page one and the header “What Is ALYMSYS® (bevacizumab-maly)?” on page two suggest monotherapy in all indications and list broad types of cancer with imagery; limitations of use not presented until page four.
cases.context: Full indications only in ISI in small plain font after eye-catching graphics.
cases.rationale: Suggests general use across cancers or as single agent.
cases.check: Rule: indication statements must include combination-therapy requirements, populations, and limitations of use at first mention.

cases.claim: Page four infusion presentation fails to disclose infusion-related reactions and suggests Alymsys “will be administered” regardless of IRR; page five: “Before receiving your ALYMSYS® treatment, tell your doctor if you: o Are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or plan to start a family in the future o Are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed …” without disclosing fetal harm, contraception, lactation, ovarian failure; omits “Withhold for at least 28 days prior to elective surgery” and arterial thromboembolic events.
cases.context: ISI presents only W&P headings without material detail; 'see page 7 for ISI' statement does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Omits material risk information and creates misleading impression of safety.
cases.check: Rule: each W&P must include its key consequence/action (not just the heading); check pregnancy/lactation, IRR, and surgery-related instructions are present.

cases.claim: “It’s likely that you will experience side effects from your ALYMSYS® treatment. This is normal, and most side effects will resolve over time.”
cases.context: Serious, sometimes fatal risks; 8%-22% discontinued for adverse reactions; cited ACS reference not product-specific. Risk not in severity order; complex medical terminology in consumer piece.
cases.rationale: Suggests all side effects resolve; minimizes serious risks.
cases.check: Does reassuring language about side effects ('normal', 'will resolve') minimize serious or fatal risks in the label?

cases.cat: Unsubstantiated superiority / comparative claims (biosimilar vs reference)
cases.claim: The totality of omissions and minimization misleadingly represents Alymsys as safer and more effective than the bevacizumab reference listed drug (AVASTIN® (bevacizumab)).
cases.context: Biosimilar approval means no clinically meaningful differences from Avastin.
cases.rationale: Any suggestion that a biosimilar is safer/more effective than its reference product is misleading.
cases.check: For biosimilars, does the piece imply safety/efficacy advantages over the reference product (explicitly or via omitted risks)?
